speaker: thomas_pope
text: Throw the feathers in with the ticking, master, and you have my silver. I'll not carry an empty bolster back to Shoreditch.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: He has thrown them in, Tom. Take the bundle under your arm before the crowd sweeps us past the spits. Sam has stood before this cutler's board longer than we shall spend at dinner.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: The knife has a horn haft, Master Phillips, and the whistle has three holes like a pipe. If I buy the knife I have nothing to blow on, and if I buy the whistle I cannot pare an apple.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thou hast sixpence to spend on one thing, Sam, and the pork is coming off the spit behind us. Choose the whistle, and leave the blades on the board.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Aye, take the whistle, boy. Between the broadcloth alleys, the hobby-horses, the ballads, the rattles, the drums, and a calf with five legs shown for a penny, there is noise enough here to drown a pipe.

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: There, he has given the woman his sixpence for the whistle, and he is still looking back at the knife as if he had left a sweetheart behind.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: Listen to the low note on it, Master Shakespeare.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: We hear it, lad. Sit you down at the trestle. Sixpenny trenchers of pork with damson sauce all round, and mind your pockets when the prentices push by.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: My hand has not left my purse since we came through the cloth-alleys. Every third elbow in this lane belongs to a man who is not looking at the stalls.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Give me that bone, Sam. Thou hast gnawed the pork off it down to the marrow, and if thou crackest the knuckle with thy teeth thou'lt have no voice for Moth tomorrow.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: There was a strip of crackling left on the side, Master Phillips.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: It is gone now. Wipe thy chin and keep thy sixpenny whistle out of the damson sauce.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Hear that drum beyond the charcoal trough? That is the puppet booth starting its next quarter-hour.

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: A penny at the cloth, sir, and a wooden devil with a club.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Let the pork settle before we go into the crush. Nobody is conning a line tonight, and tomorrow at two we have a house to open.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Have you seen Kemp since we passed the sheep-pens, Dick?

speaker: richard_burbage
text: He went off toward the horse-fair when the rattles started. We shall find him where the hats are thickest.

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: Watch your bolster against the grease-trough, Master Pope!

speaker: thomas_pope
text: It is high and dry on my shoulder, boy. Come on, let us see what the puppets do for a penny.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: Thank you for the sixpence, Master Phillips.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Keep it inside thy doublet, Sam, and stay between Tom and me in the alley.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Hand on the purse, and slow through the ropes.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Look at the sea of hats round that striped canvas ahead of us.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Every apprentice within the walls is here, and we shall have them all in the yard tomorrow afternoon.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Lead on to the booth, Dick.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Between us, Sam. The whistle stays in the doublet.
